chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother Musa (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man, is it permissible for him to stand at 'Arafat without wudu? He said: 'It is not permissible unless he is upon wudu.'

key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: 'Arafat (the plain where the main standing of Hajj occurs)

ai.seo_question: Is wudu required for standing at Arafat during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), the requirement of ritual purity (wudu) during the standing at 'Arafat is established as a condition for the validity of the pillar itself, not merely a recommended act. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence as it underscores the spiritual and physical preparedness required for the climax of Hajj, distinguishing it from the general permissibility of performing Hajj with minor impurities in other contexts. The emphasis on wudu reflects the sanctity of the moment of standing before God, aligning with the broader Islamic principle of approaching the Divine in a state of cleanliness.
